title: The Capacitor That Drew Too Much Current
featured_title: THE CAPACITOR THAT DREW TOO MUCH CURRENT
subject: electrical-computer
audience: FE Electrical and Computer candidates and engineering students

presentation.challenge: The steady-state current is zero. At switch-on, the circuit violates its 5 mA startup limit.

practice.primary_question: Why can an initially uncharged capacitor draw its highest current immediately after a DC source is connected?
practice.typical_exam_trap: Applying the capacitor open-circuit DC steady-state rule at the switching instant instead of using the initial capacitor voltage.

case_dna.target_misconception: A capacitor is an open circuit for DC, so current must be zero from the instant a DC source is connected.
case_dna.why_plausible: The capacitor open-circuit rule is correct only at DC steady state. It is easy to apply that final condition too early and ignore capacitor-voltage continuity at the switching instant.
case_dna.contradicting_evidence: The initially uncharged capacitor has 0 V at t = 0+, so the 1 kΩ resistor initially sees the full 10 V and carries 10 mA.
case_dna.corrected_model: Use the capacitor's initial voltage at t = 0+ before applying the steady-state model. For an initially uncharged RC circuit, i(0+) = V/R and the current then decays exponentially with time constant RC.

problem_statement: A 10 V DC source is connected through a 1 kΩ resistor to an initially uncharged 1000 µF capacitor. The design review says the capacitor is an open circuit on DC, so the branch current should be zero. In testing, the startup current reaches 10 mA, exceeding a 5 mA design requirement. Diagnose the missing initial-condition check, calculate the time constant, and choose a resistor that satisfies the startup-current limit.
fixed_constraints: Startup current must not exceed 5 mA

gates.label: Incident
gates.heading: DC says zero current. Startup says otherwise.
gates.prompt: If a capacitor is an open circuit at DC steady state, why is the switch-on current nonzero?

gates.label: Theory
gates.heading: Commit a startup model before the trace appears

options.label: The capacitor is an open circuit immediately, so current should start at 0 mA
options.reason: The open-circuit model describes DC steady state, not the switching instant. An initially uncharged capacitor starts with 0 V across it.

options.label: The uncharged capacitor starts at 0 V, so the resistor initially sees the full source voltage
options.reason: Capacitor voltage cannot change instantaneously. At t = 0+, Vc = 0 V, so the resistor initially has 10 V across it.

options.label: The capacitor is permanently a short circuit on DC
options.reason: The capacitor behaves like a short only as an initial-condition approximation for an ideal uncharged capacitor at the instant of switching; its voltage then rises and current decays.

options.label: The 10 mA pulse proves the source voltage is too high
options.reason: The 10 mA value follows directly from 10 V / 1 kΩ and is expected from the stated initial condition.

gates.label: Predict
gates.heading: Predict the current at t = 0+
gates.prompt: For an initially uncharged capacitor, what current (mA) flows immediately after the switch closes?

gates.label: Experiment
gates.heading: Close the switch and capture the first instant
gates.result: At t = 0+, the branch current is 10 mA. It then decays toward zero as the capacitor charges.

gates.label: Gap
gates.heading: Prove the startup current
gates.prompt: At t = 0+, the uncharged capacitor has 0 V. Use i(0+) = V/R with V = 10 V and R = 1 kΩ. Enter the initial current in mA.
gates.success: i(0+) = 10 V / 1 kΩ = 10 mA. The time constant is τ = RC = 1 s.
gates.hint: Use the capacitor's initial voltage first; the resistor initially sees the full 10 V.

gates.label: Evidence
gates.heading: The transient trace resolves the contradiction

cards.text: Capacitor voltage at t = 0+ is 0 V because the capacitor is initially uncharged.
Initial resistor voltage is 10 V, giving i(0+) = 10 V / 1 kΩ = 10 mA.
τ = RC = (1 kΩ)(1000 µF) = 1 s; current decays toward 0 mA only with time.

gates.label: Redline
gates.heading: Correct the startup review
report: C1. The source is 10 V DC and the series resistor is 1 kΩ.
C2. The capacitor is initially uncharged.
C3. Because a capacitor is an open circuit on DC, branch current is 0 mA from the instant the switch closes.

claims.label: C1
claims.reason: C1 is a stated circuit condition.

claims.label: C2
claims.reason: C2 is the stated initial condition and is essential to the transient calculation.

claims.label: C3
claims.reason: C3 applies the steady-state capacitor model at t = 0+. Initially Vc = 0 V, so current starts at 10 mA.

evidence_choices.label: The final DC current approaches 0 mA
evidence_choices.reason: That confirms the steady-state model but does not explain the startup-limit violation.

evidence_choices.label: Vc(0+) = 0 V and i(0+) = 10 V / 1 kΩ = 10 mA
evidence_choices.reason: This directly proves why the startup current is nonzero and exceeds the 5 mA requirement.

evidence_choices.label: The capacitor value is 1000 µF
evidence_choices.reason: Capacitance sets the time constant, but the initial current for this ideal RC case is set by source voltage and series resistance.

correction.template: The capacitor starts at {initial_v} V, so the branch current starts at {initial_i} mA and only later decays toward zero.

gates.label: Design Fix
gates.heading: Meet the 5 mA startup-current limit
gates.constraint: Keep the 10 V source and 1000 µF capacitor. Startup current must be no more than 5 mA.

options.label: Increase the series resistance to at least 2 kΩ
options.reason: R ≥ V/Imax = 10 V / 5 mA = 2 kΩ. With 2 kΩ, startup current is 5 mA and τ becomes 2 s.

options.label: Reduce the series resistance to 500 Ω
options.reason: That doubles startup current to 20 mA and makes the violation worse.

options.label: Keep 1 kΩ because the final current is zero
options.reason: The requirement applies at startup, when the 1 kΩ circuit draws 10 mA.

options.label: Increase capacitance while leaving the resistor at 1 kΩ
options.reason: In the ideal RC model, changing capacitance changes the time constant but not i(0+) = V/R.

gates.label: Transfer
gates.heading: Apply the initial-condition rule to a new RC circuit
gates.prompt: A 12 V source is connected through 3 kΩ to an initially uncharged capacitor. What is the initial current?

options.label: 4 mA
options.reason: At t = 0+, the capacitor voltage is 0 V, so i = 12 V / 3 kΩ = 4 mA.

options.label: 0 mA
options.reason: Zero current is the ideal DC steady-state result, not the initial value for an uncharged capacitor.

options.label: 36 mA
options.reason: Ohm's law requires division, not multiplication: 12 V / 3 kΩ = 4 mA.

options.label: It cannot be known without the capacitance
options.reason: For an ideal initially uncharged series RC circuit, i(0+) = V/R; capacitance determines how fast the current decays.

gates.explanation: An initially uncharged ideal capacitor starts at 0 V, so the series resistor initially sees the full source voltage.

gates.label: Sign Off
gates.heading: Sign off the transient analysis
gates.confirmation: I confirm that the DC steady-state capacitor model must not be applied at t = 0+ without checking the capacitor's initial voltage.

items.label: What violated the limit
items.value: The initially uncharged capacitor made the 1 kΩ resistor carry 10 mA at t = 0+.

items.label: What was missed
items.value: The open-circuit capacitor rule is a DC steady-state result, not the switching-instant model.

items.label: Corrected model
items.value: Use capacitor-voltage continuity first, then calculate i(0+) and the RC time constant.

seo.excerpt: A capacitor is open-circuit at DC steady state, but that does not mean startup current is zero. Diagnose a 10 mA switch-on current in an RC circuit.
seo.direct_answer: An initially uncharged capacitor has 0 V across it at t = 0+, so a series resistor initially sees the full source voltage. With 10 V and 1 kΩ, the initial current is 10 mA; it then decays exponentially with time constant RC.

faqs.q: Why does an uncharged capacitor draw current when first connected to DC?
faqs.a: Its voltage cannot change instantaneously, so it begins at its initial voltage and the series resistor initially carries current set by the source voltage and resistance.
